prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor checkout counter layout where a red shopping basket (~0.4–0.6 m away, bottom right) and the camera wearer's hand holding a green bottle in frame 5 (~0.3–0.4 m away) are the brightest, nearest elements within the camera wearer's immediate arm's reach. Slightly further in front (~0.7–1.2 m) are the checkout register on the lower left, a standing brown paper bag on the counter, and a person in a blue polo shirt standing behind the counter (~1.0–1.5 m away, ~0.3–0.5 m from the bag), while a doorway frame on the right (~0.8–1.2 m) separates the foreground from a second person in a plaid shirt (~2.5–3.5 m away on the far left of frame 2, ~2 m left of the counter) and distant store shelving (>4 m, dark background). Across the 5 frames, the person in blue stays at roughly ~1.0–1.5 m but turns his torso from angled toward the front-left register (frames 1–2) to profile facing the bag on his right (frames 3–4) before facing forward toward the camera wearer in frame 5 as the camera wearer's right hand and bottle enter from the bottom right. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground doorframe, counter, and paper bag from the deep store background through the open doorway, and confirms the raised package in frame 3 is at roughly the same depth plane as the bag opening. However, the map is unreliable along the open mesh of the red basket—which it fills as a solid bright slab—and it flattens internal facial details and glass panes into uniform grey regions.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and background instances against a black void, consistently detecting the person in the blue shirt (~1.0–1.5 m in front, right of center, waist-up behind the counter) and a small bottle on the counter (~1.0 m away, lower left, ~0.5 m left of the person) across all 5 frames. In frame 2, it captures the second person in the plaid shirt (~2.5–3.5 m away, facing away into the background aisle on the far left and partly cut off by the left frame edge), and in frame 5 it segments the green bottle held within ~0.3–0.5 m in the camera wearer's bottom-right reach alongside a tiny blue 'person' fragment at the lower-left edge (from frame 4's right edge). Across frames 1 to 5, the primary person's mask shows his silhouette rotating from facing front-left while holding a box (which leaves a black unsegmented hole inside his chest mask in frame 1) to facing left in profile with arms extended toward the unsegmented paper bag (frames 3–4), and finally facing the camera wearer in frame 5 while his left hand and the wearer's hand overlap the green bottle. While segmentation makes the tiny bottle by the register and the distant left-edge person stand out more sharply than in the cluttered RGB view, it is highly unreliable for scene layout and objects: it completely omits the counter, walls, brown paper bag, and handheld package, and mislabels the foreground red shopping basket (~0.5 m below the person) as a 'chair' in frames 3–5 and distant shelves (>4 m away on the left) as 'book' and 'banana' in frames 1–2.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D body (yellow) and hand (magenta) skeletons only for the person in the blue shirt (~1.0–1.5 m in front of the camera wearer), omitting all background structures, objects, the distant person in frame 2, and the camera wearer's own arm in frame 5. The facial keypoint clusters above the shoulder line track his head orientation across time: angled downward and to the camera's left toward the register and handheld box in frames 1–2, turned into a left-facing profile looking at the paper bag area in frames 3–4 as his torso rectangle narrows almost to a vertical line, and oriented straight toward the camera wearer in frame 5. His arm and hand keypoints trace what is within his ~0.5–0.7 m reach: in frames 1–2, his right arm extends down-left to the register while his left elbow bends to hold the box at chest height; in frame 3, both wrists lift upward to the left above the bag opening; in frame 4, his left arm reaches down-left onto the counter; and in frame 5, his right hand rests near the counter while his left wrist extends down-right to within ~0.2 m of the camera wearer's bottle. This skeleton view makes his 3D torso rotation, shoulder-width collapse in profile (frames 3–4), and occluded back-arm trajectory much easier to read than in RGB alone. However, the map is unreliable below the waist (clipped by the counter occlusion), misses the distant person in frame 2 and the camera wearer's hand in frame 5, and fails to detect magenta finger keypoints whenever the hands move rapidly or are partially occluded in frames 3, 4, and the left hand of frame 5.
